props.title: Maniac

sections.content: Maniac represents a bold reimagining of William Lustig's 1980 slasher film, with Elijah Wood's chilling performance as Frank Zito marking a dramatic departure from his hobbit-next-door persona. Shot almost entirely in first-person POV like Lady in the Lake (1947), but with a modern digital twist, the film forces viewers into the mind of a disturbed killer. This innovative perspective creates an unsettling intimacy that surpasses even the psychological horror of American Psycho (2000), making us unwilling participants in Frank's violent compulsions. Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer|1986|A devastating character study of a murderer that strips away Hollywood glamorization|Tubi Peeping Tom|1960|Groundbreaking psychological horror about a cameraman who films his victims' deaths|Criterion Don't Breathe|2016|Subversive home invasion thriller that plays with perspective and morality|Netflix

The film's technical achievements deserve special attention. Director Franck Khalfoun and cinematographer Maxime Alexandre crafted ingenious solutions for the POV format, using mirrors and reflections to reveal Wood's face at crucial moments. This technique echoes the mirror motif in Black Christmas (1974) and Dressed to Kill (1980), but pushes it into new territory. The pulsing electronic score by Rob evokes both Drive (2011) and vintage Argento films like Tenebrae (1982), creating a neo-giallo atmosphere that perfectly matches the neon-lit Los Angeles setting.

The mannequin motif throughout Maniac connects to a rich history of horror films exploring objectification and artificial humanity, from Eyes Without a Face (1960) to Tourist Trap (1979). Frank's relationship with Anna (Nora Arnezeder) adds layers of complexity, reminiscent of the psychological depth in The Silence of the Lambs (1991) but with a more intimate, devastating impact. Behind the Mask: The Rise of Leslie Vernon|2006|Meta-horror that deconstructs slasher film tropes through mockumentary|Shudder May|2002|Character-driven horror about loneliness and obsession|AMC+ The House That Jack Built|2018|Controversial serial killer character study with artistic pretensions|Hulu SUBHEAD: Modern POV Horror Evolution

Maniac helped pave the way for more experimental first-person horror like Hardcore Henry (2015) and segments of V/H/S (2012). Its influence can be seen in the subjective camera work of You're Next (2011) and the psychological intimacy of The Eyes of My Mother (2016), showing how technical innovation can serve character development in horror.
